about: The one source for stadium and tabletop colour and motion. fantasyedge/scene.py embeds it in every scene as `palette`, tools/make_tokens.py writes fantasyedge/templates/tokens.css from it, and the visionOS app bundles this file unchanged. Edit here, never in a copy.

chip.about: A team colour is kept as its hue and solved into one relative-luminance band, so white text on any club's chip clears 4.5:1. The band and rule match Theme.chipFill.

arc.about: Apex heights in yards. d is the yards the ball travelled along the field. A pass peaks at 3 + 0.35d, a run at 0.8 + 0.12d.

goalKick.about: Field goals and extra points aim at the uprights on the end line the kicking side attacks (scene.goal_kick): a good kick ends overshootYards past the posts on the centre line; a wide miss ends wideYards outside the upright on the side the play text names; a short one ends shortYards in front of them.

motion.about: Real-time play durations are clamped to [minSeconds, maxSeconds]. A replay faster than referenceSpeed divides them by speed / referenceSpeed, never below floorSeconds, so a play finishes before the next snap arrives. momentSeconds is how long a celebration stays up, and it starts when the ball lands, not when the play arrives: the composer holds a moment until Broadcast has flown it, giving up after the play's own flight plus momentHoldGraceSeconds so a scene with no such play can never strand one. The drawn score, down and red-zone flag lag the scene the same way (StatusGate): a status describes the state after its play, so it is held until that play lands, with the same grace as a deadline.

visual.about: Visual-only parameters, one section per stadium actor (docs/ART_BIBLE.md). Nothing here changes where anything is. Asset paths are relative to assets/: generated/<actor>/ holds what tools/make_assets.py writes, actors/<actor>/ holds a specialist's authored assets. A section may name another actor's file; models are .usdz for Apple with a .glb sibling for web and Android.

camera.about: The wearer's eyes above the floor of the space, and how long a seat change fades.

tabletop.about: The table model is an architect's cutaway: the stands on the near (home) sideline are left out between these fractions of a half turn, so the wearer looks into the bowl.

arrival.about: Tabletop to seat. A curtain of stadium light rises from the plinth's edge and widens over the table while the table dims, then the space opens on the Crown dial. The world never moves the wearer's head. Reduce motion: no curtain, the space opens at once.

layout.about: Every panel in the stadium as yaw (degrees, + right), flat distance (m) and height above the eye (m, - below). From a lower-bowl seat the field of play sits about 9-30 degrees below the eye, so side panels sit low and peripheral, the controls lowest, the scorebug above the far stands. tests/test_experience.py holds each slot inside maxSideDegrees and maxBelowDegrees. These slots are defaults for a scene without per-seat layout: scene.py's seat_panels() lays every panel out per seat as a dock (see dock), and the scene carries the result as layout.perSeat.

panelSizes.about: The contract for each panel's footprint in points: widthPoints exactly, maxHeightPoints at most. The stadium clamps each panel to it, the silhouette test uses it (at pointsPerMeter), and a renderer drawing inside a panel (Broadcast's drive log) must fit it.

scorebugYield.about: The glass scorebug yields to the stadium's video board when the board carries the score legibly from the seat: its face turned toward the wearer, within inViewDegrees of straight ahead, and subtending at least boardMinDegrees across. The scene says per seat as layout.perSeat.<seat>.scorebugHidden.

dock.about: The dock: one anchored layer, laid out the same way from every seat (scene.py seat_panels). The rail holds the Drive tab, the Controls pill and the right-hand tab on one line at rail.distance, gapDegrees apart, in the lowest clear band of the comfort window, at the height nearest rail.preferredBelowDegrees. The gallery holds opened panels: the side panels as a mirrored pair between gallery.minSideDegrees and maxSideDegrees, at the nearest of minDistance..maxDistance (distanceStep) whose angle fits, preferring comfortableBelowDegrees; distanceCost and inwardCost weigh going further out and toward the centre. The controls open within controls.maxYawDegrees of centre, minDistance..maxDistance, nearest the pill. Hard rules, never costs: off the painted field - surface, end zones and the painted border, plus paintClearYards of ground beyond it (fieldMarginDegrees on top), the video board, the ribbon and the rim light banks; the panel's centre inside maxSideDegrees and its whole box inside viewWindowDegrees, so no element is half out of view, above maxBelowDegrees and below highestBelowDegrees (negative is above the eye); and nearer, by nearClearanceMeters, than any chair, rail, ground or glass it overlaps, drawn smaller by `scale` when that brings it in, never nearer than minDistance. A panel with nowhere its full height fits is shortened first - down to gallery.minHeightFraction of maxHeightPoints in heightStep steps, at heightCost each, which costs rows rather than type size, and the scene ships the seat's own maxHeightPoints - and only then drawn smaller, down to gallery.minScale at scaleCost a step. However it is moved, shortened or scaled, a panel subtends at least what it would full size at gallery.maxDistance.

recentre.about: A tap on the Controls pill, or a pinch anywhere in the room, re-seats the dock in front of where the wearer is looking now. The scene solves the dock again for each facing bucketDegrees apart out to maxYawDegrees either side, so every rule holds from the new facing; the app picks the bucket nearest the head's yaw and fades the dock across in fadeSeconds (reduce motion: no fade). Recentring while facing the seat's own forward lands on bucket 0, which is the layout the seat started with, so the gesture is its own undo.

panels.about: Side panels fold to a 60-point tab and unfold on a tap; the elsewhere panel lists elsewhereRows games. During a celebrated moment every panel folds and its tab fades to momentOpacity over momentFadeSeconds (reduce motion: folds, no fade), leaving only the scorebug and Broadcast's banner; momentReturnSeconds after the banner goes each panel returns as the wearer had it.

controls.about: The bottom panel: play and scrub, speed, replay drive, seat, mute, immersion, leave. It folds to one 60-point pill after autoHideSeconds without a touch and returns on a tap of the pill or a pinch on the field (the reveal catcher, an invisible target this far out).

seatPicker.about: A map of the bowl drawn from bowl.shape and presentation.stadium.seats beside a list of the same seats; every seat is a 60-point target in both.

field.about: Field actor. Turf is a 0.40 m tile of baked blades, the two mowing-stripe meshes wearing the with- and against-the-mower normals. Paint is a signed distance field thresholded at `paint.threshold`, one half-canvas texture per colour drawn twice under a half turn about midfield (assets/actors/field/README.md). Art layout comes from scene.field.art.

perLeague.about: Loaded by the actor for scene.field.markings; paths are relative to that folder's league.

sideline.about: Sideline actor. Every static prop is merged into one mesh per palette entry (team-tinted entries once per club); the chains and the down box are a second, small merge rebuilt when the line to gain moves. Placement is along a team area's centre, `offset` yards beyond the sideline.

lodSuffix.about: Which mesh each prop draws. `stadium` is the default and `tabletop` the whole model set at table size. `stadiumByModel` names the props the stadium draws at LOD1 instead: the team-area dressing, which is 40+ yd from every seat and was drawing its full mesh because LOD1 was exported and used by nothing. The objects a viewer reads - goal posts, pylons, the chain crew, the benches at the field-level seat - keep their full mesh.

bowl.about: The kit from tools/blender/bowl: stands, far seat bands with a fill per seat preset, a foreground patch per preset, and the table model. Authored in metres; the actor scales by 1/yardMeters. seatColor tints every seat. rows and segments drive the crowd's rows, the procedural fallback and the sideline boards.

crowd.about: Fans come from the Blender crowd kit (tools/blender/crowd, assets/actors/crowd/manifest.json). Near the wearer they are real meshes frozen in poses (lod0, lod1); farther out, multi-angle impostor cards. Clothing is tinted per matchup from the kit's mask: R the club chip, G `secondary`, B face paint. Fans move by group: a group swaps pose (a mesh, or an atlas row), never skins per fan on the CPU. The away section is bowl.crowd.awaySection. About a third of each section wears no club colour (`neutrals`), and every fan's club colour takes its own value and saturation, so a stand is a mass, not two flat hues. Far cards are softened toward each fan's mean (`cardContrast`) and split into interleaved `cardVariants` per slice with jittered edges, so a pose change never draws a vertical stripe.

impostor.floodFillAbout: Far cards are flat quads a hundred metres from the lamps and pick up almost none of the floods, so stands measured about four stops under the field against lighting.response.fieldStopsAboveStands 1. Each card emits its own dressed colour at this emissive intensity (RealityKit's scale: 0.45 blew the stands to white), standing in for the flood spill on a real bowl. Near meshes are lit and take none.

clearance.about: No fan within `radius` yards of any seat on the flat, or `height` yards of its floor, so nobody stands in the wearer's lap.

chair.about: How a fan meets Bowl's chair, whose origin is the feet on the tread facing +z (tools/blender/bowl/seat.py): pan at 0.43 m, back at z -0.22 m. The kit's seated pelvis is 0.30 m behind its feet at 0.52 m for a 1.75 m fan. Seated poses move forward `sitForwardMetres` (0.20 pushed knees past the tread edge in the steep upper deck) and lift so every fan's pelvis rests at `pelvisMetres`; standing poses move forward `standForwardMetres`, clear of the folded pan. Cards use `cardForwardMetres`, between the two. Measured by tools/blender/crowd/seat_fit.py: at 0.52 hips sank 1.5-7.5 cm into the pan; at 0.55 they meet it. Seated ankles are solved to `ankleForwardMetres` in front of the chair's origin (mh.solve_legs), which keeps the whole shoe inside Bowl's `seating.feetDepth` of tread: at integration-12 the nearest fan's shoes hung over the edge above the row below.

rings.about: Distance from the wearer's seat in yards. Nearest first, up to each cap: lod0, lod1, lod2, lod3 meshes, then paired cards. The caps are the crowd's triangle budget and they set how far the mesh circle reaches - they no longer decide mesh against card, because a row seen end-on holds more fans inside the mesh radius than they allow and the overflow stood among solid fans as flat billboards. Whoever is nearest is a mesh; `minCardYards` is the floor that circle can never fall below. Round 10: the circle is bought in fans, and 250 triangles was the price of one. A fourth tier at 120 buys two fans for the price of one lod2, so lod2Max 145 -> 40 and lod3Max 286 take the circle from 183 fans to 364 - 7.6 yd to about 10.5 at the club seat, where every fan in view had been a flat card. 14 x 3000 + 24 x 900 + 40 x 250 + 286 x 120 = 107.9k, inside the 108k left by the crowd's measured 40.3k of cards (docs/actors/crowd.md, round 10).

clubValue.about: The crowd wears the club's *stated* colour (teams.*.color), never the panel chip: a chip is solved for white text on a card and is a different colour. The only thing the stand is allowed to move is HSV value - r, g and b scaled together, which cannot shift a hue - and only up to this floor. Field paint is one flat plane and returns one radiance; a stand is thousands of fabric surfaces at every angle, plus hats, sleeves, forearms and faces, so the same dye reads lighter and, more to the point, reads as many surfaces. The floor is where it stops reading as many: measured in round 9 by sweeping it on a black club and reading the stand's own pixels bowl-wide (docs/actors/crowd.md). Neutrals are not lifted; a club already above the floor is worn exactly as stated.

tint.about: Material brightness per group: `normal`; the scoring side `bright`; the other side `dim` while a moment is on. Near meshes are lit, so they dim less than cards (`meshDim`): 0.3 on a lit body under a coloured strobe read black.

crowd.castShadowsAbout: Fans do not cast flood shadows: 45k merged fans shadowed Bowl's treads to black and cost shadow-pass draws. Contact shading comes from the kit's baked occlusion.
crowd.nearMixAbout: Near rings only. Each slot CrowdChoreography.slot returns is one merged mesh per group; in it every fan wears a pose drawn by that fan's own seat hash from these shares, so a group changing slot changes some people and not others. Chatting pairs turn to each other in `sit` at chatShare.
crowd.supportAbout: Whose crowd it is. A home game is overwhelmingly the home club's colours. The visitors get a core block behind their own bench and a thinner tail into the upper corners, chosen from the scene: bowl.crowd.awaySection first, then field.props.benches, then the corners on that side, until `visitingShare` of the bowl's sections carry them. Inside that, support is drawn per seat in blocks of `blockRows` x `blockSeats`, at `coreProbability` in the middle of the block falling to `edgeProbability` at its edge, so the boundary is ragged and a few home shirts sit inside the visiting block and a few visitors outside it. A whole section cannot be one colour: at integration-13 it read as a painted wedge. `neutralShare` more sections wear neither club. Support still cannot vary freely per seat - a group of fans shares one texture, so the cost is the number of (slice, support, variant) groups, which is why only sections with a pull host visitors at all.
crowd.emptySeatsAbout: Empty seats, because a sold-out bowl with every seat filled reads as wallpaper. `base` scales everywhere, the upper deck keeps fewer than the lower, and the corners fewer than midfield. A thinned block empties from its middle outwards (`aislePull`): the seats by an aisle go first in a stand and empty last, so what is left is a ragged edge along the gangway rather than a scatter. `blowout` uses what the scene knows - status.homeScore, awayScore, period and clock - to empty the upper deck late in a decided game; the scene carries no attendance, so nothing else is inferred.
crowd.reactionsAbout: What a crowd does, beyond cheering. On third down the defending side rises (`thirdDownStand`) and the side whose offence is at the line goes quiet (`hushOwnOffence`): a home crowd does not roar at its own snap count. A visiting score is real but outnumbered, so the visitors' celebration is smaller (`visitorCelebration`), and the scored-on side still never celebrates.
crowd.momentRippleAbout: A section that brightens as one rectangle advertises itself as a rectangle. Each group's tint rises over `tintRiseSeconds` after its own ripple delay, at its own pace (`tintRiseSpread`), and settles at its own brightness (`tintJitter`): at integration-14 the blocks rose in turn and still ended level, which put the rectangle back at the end of the moment.

lighting.about: The light: probe, rim banks (modelled in tools/blender/lighting, merged into one draw per material), glows, beams, haze layers, floods, strobe and wash. `response` is the look every other actor lights against; it is documentation for them, not read by Lighting.

rim.about: Banks at angle k*pi/(count/2) + phase around the bowl. Banks with z <= farSideMaxZ face the seats and get the near model; the rest stand behind the wearer and get the far model. bowl.rimLights.side 'far' draws only the first kind.

beams.about: One quad per beam from the banks you face, turned about its own axis toward the seat and re-laid when the wearer changes seat, drawn only where it hangs over the field: each starts where its ray comes inside the bowl at startInsideOffsetYards, so no additive light lies across the stands. Beams are dropped, farthest first, until their summed screen coverage from the seat (projected area over distance squared, per 2.4 sr of view) is under overdrawCapScreens.

facing.about: Integration-11: the crossed pair became one seat-facing quad, which covers the same shaft with about 60% of the fill. Under the graph's |N.V|^viewPower a crossed pair at a random roll sums to about 0.85 of one face-on quad, so the graph's opacity scales by shaderOpacityScale; the UV-scroll fallback has no view falloff and drew two overlapping layers, so it scales by fallbackOpacityScale. trimU is the part of the beam texture each side whose alpha stays under 3% of the row's peak (24 of 256 texels): the quad stops there. A port still drawing crossed quads ignores this block.

shader.about: The beam as a Shader Graph (tools/blender/lighting/shadergraph/Beams.rkassets, compiled by shadergraph.py). alpha = profile(u,v) * (dustFloor + dustAmount * dust(u, v*dustRepeat + t*dustSpeed)) * |N.V|^viewPower * opacity; colour premultiplied, additive when additive = 1. A client without the graph draws the UV-scroll beam and dust above (opacity, dustOpacity, dustTileYards, dustScrollPerSecond). Strobe gain and wash tint apply to opacity and color.

elevationFade.about: Beam and dust alpha scale by the seat's angle of depression to the field centre: 1 below fromDegrees, minScale above toDegrees, smoothstep between. Looking down along the shafts stacks the crossed quads into sheets.

haze.about: Faint rings of lit air round the rim, at the banks' height and outside the field's sky, stadium only. The band texture fades at both edges (v 0 inner, 1 outer); u repeats round the bowl.

strobe.about: Multipliers at the peak of a strobe (Moments sets shared.strobeUntil). Lenses and glows pulse to their gain; beams, dust, haze and the spill over the seats never exceed beamGainMax / hazeGainMax, so the stands keep their colour; the floods on the field rise to fieldWashGain.

fill.about: Concourse fill: warm light from the concourse and vomitories on the seat-facing back of the upper deck's guard wall, from the walkway up to Bowl's LED strip (offset and rise mirror tools/blender/bowl/structure.py wall_b, walk and cap), and in the tunnel mouths. An unlit additive band, one draw, no light.

sky.about: The night: star dome, a thin drifting veil of cloud, and the warm light dome the floodlit bowl throws above its rim. Stadium only.

trail.about: A flight trail is a camera-facing filament of light with a soft halo, faint at the snap and full where the ball came down. The newest play is bright; older plays of the drive ghost and thin by `age` per play.

tail.about: Alpha along the trail: `opacity` at the snap rising as u^power to 1 where the play ended. Baked into trail_core.png and trail_halo.png by tools/blender/broadcast/textures.py.

age.about: The newest `individual` plays draw one by one: opacity x decay^age (never under minOpacity), width x thin^age (never under minScale). Older plays merge into one ghost in `historyColor` at `historyOpacity`, so the back of a long drive costs two draw parts, not two per play. Raised at round 8: with the night dropped two stops the drive behind the newest play had faded under the grass it lies on, and a drive read as one arc rather than as a drive.

nearSeat.about: A trail within `yards` of the seat thins in proportion, never below `minScale` of its core.

edge.about: A trail seen along its own length - a kick from behind the posts - reads as a streak. Its opacity and width scale by how side-on the seat sees it (BroadcastTrails.sideOn: the mean angle between the arc and the sightline), from minOpacity and minScale at goneDegrees to whole at fullDegrees. Only `shapes` fade, which is kicks: runs and penalties hug the grass, and a pass now flies from the quarterback to where it was caught, often across the field toward a sideline seat - fading it would hide the play being watched.

kick.about: A kick laid while watching fades to restOpacity over fadeSeconds, so it reads in flight and does not stand over the posts after; reduce motion lands it at rest. A kick stands tall, so its side-on fade uses its own fullDegrees and goneDegrees in place of edge's.

live.about: The play in the air draws its trail behind the ball as far as it has flown, at `opacity`, redrawn at most every `intervalSeconds`; on landing it is replaced by the laid trail. Without it a trail appeared only when the ball came down, and a kick had faded before anyone saw it cross the posts.

lowSeat.about: Plays already done lie lower for a seat whose eye is below their flight: no higher than `apexOverEye` of the eye's height above the field, never under `minApexYards`. From the field and the front rows a drive's passes otherwise stand over the far stands as a wall of arches. The newest play keeps the height the scene gave it. A lowered ghost of the drive's back half draws at `historyOpacity`.

glow.about: The light on the ball. Its world size grows with the distance to the wearer so it never falls below `minArcMinutes` at the eye (capped at `maxYards`), and it sits `coverYards` toward the wearer so that far away the light covers the dark leather instead of ringing it: at 100 yd the ball itself is a speck under a third of a degree wide, and a halo around it reads as a dark dot.

flight.about: How the ball moves along an arc. A play picks a manner by its style, then its type, then its shape: `spiral` rolls about the long axis, `wobble` adds a precession, `tumble` turns end over end, `carry` is tucked and bobbing, `bounce` runs the arc and then bounds, as a fumble does.

ball.about: The ball is drawn at life size where the wearer can see that it is a ball, and magnified only far enough away that it would otherwise be a speck: `scale` is reached at `farYards`, life size holds within `nearYards`, and it eases between. Before this it was 2.6x life size everywhere - about a yard long in the hands of a club seat, which is a cartoon (art bible: findable at fifty yards without being one). Its light, not its size, is what makes it findable now.

laser.about: The TV lines: light painted onto the grass, not a neon tube over it. Feathered at the edges with blades of grass standing through, never lifted far enough to float.

texture.about: line.png: `feather` is the share of the width each soft edge takes; `grass` is how much the blades break it up.

tag.about: The down-and-distance tag painted on the far half of the field beside the line of scrimmage, inside the yard numbers and short of the hash, reading toward the seat.

horizon.about: Win probability as one luminous band above the far rim: thicker the more one side is favoured, tinted toward that side's chip, faded at both ends, with a glowing marker at now and one label beside it. The series is smoothed with a gaussian `smoothing` x its length wide before it is drawn, so one play's swing reads as a curve rather than a spike.

edge.about: The band fades by how obliquely the wearer sees it: the mean angle between its plane and the sightlines to five points along it, fully drawn at `fullDegrees` and gone at `goneDegrees`. From behind an end zone (about 32 degrees) it is gone and the video board carries win probability; from the sidelines (48 degrees and up) it is whole.

legibility.about: The ribbon's capital letters must subtend at least `minArcMinutes` from the default stadium seat to the far side of the bowl, where they are smallest. A test checks it against the scene.

scroll.about: The ribbon drifts round the bowl. Reduce motion holds it still.

flash.about: A moment takes over the whole ribbon for `seconds`: the word, in the scoring side's chip.

ribbon.about: The crawl on the upper deck's fascia. Bowl builds the fascia and a dark screen at bowl.ribbon.offset; the crawl is its own surface `offset` yards toward the field along the fascia's normal - more than the 0.1 yd chord tolerance Bowl tessellates to - cut into `segments`, so the two never z-fight.

banner.about: How the moment graphic looks: a slab in the scoring side's chip with the word and the scoreline, a soft glow behind it. What it covers and when - kinds, the timeline offset, width in degrees at the wearer, minimum height, height over the scoring end zone, dwell, enter, exit, subtitle size - is Moments' contract in visual.moments.banner. `widthYards.tabletop` applies on the table, where there is no eye to measure an angle from; `widthYards.stadium` is a fallback only.

videoBoard.about: What the video board behind the east end zone shows, on Bowl's face (bowl.videoBoard): the score across the top `scorebugShare` of its height, each club a block `sideShare` of its width with the clock between; a down-and-distance strip `downShare` high the width of the board; then the last play at the left `textShare` of its width in at most `lines` lines, and the newest `plays` plays drawn from above on a small field at the right. Every size is a share of the board's height; the smallest words are `smallTextShare` of it, and `legibility.minArcMinutes` is what their capitals must subtend from the seat farthest from the board. Drawn `offset` yards in front of Bowl's dark screen so the two never z-fight.

driveLog.about: How many plays the drive-log glass lists (`rows`, the newest last), and how many lines the newest and older plays' text may take. Experience folds the panel and passes the row count through; this is the default. Sized so the unfolded log stays a short, low panel at the side (docs/actors/experience.md).

play.about: How a play moves, the way a broadcast replay graphic draws it: scene.play_path turns a play's type, spots and text into timed segments every client flies the same way. A `hold` keeps the ball on a spot, a `carry` runs it along points at carry height, an `air` flies it on a gravity parabola whose `rise` over the chord is gravity x hang^2 / 8 x drag. Heights in yards, times in real seconds; a replay faster than motion.referenceSpeed divides them like any play. Nothing here invents a player: only where the ball went, as the text says.

run.about: The hole the text names, in yards off the snap lane toward the runner's side (facing the attack, right is +z x attack). The runner meets the hole at the line after `meshSeconds` and runs on at `yardsPerSecond`, drifting `driftShare` of the gain further toward the side.

pass.about: Air yards are not in ESPN's text: `short` and `deep` bound them, and the rest of the gain is run after the catch. Hang is `hangBase` + `hangPerYard` x the throw's length along the ground.

goalKick.about: A kick is snapped back `backYards`, held, and struck along the arc the scene states, which carries ten yards past the posts so it plainly crosses their plane. The ball and its trail stop `netYards` past that plane, where the kick leaves play: flown the whole way, a lit ball hung over the far stands with a stick-straight trail behind it (integration-12, td-moment t8.5).

marker.about: One ground card under the play: a ring that swells and fades on the snap (`pulse`), then the ball's soft shadow, smaller and fainter the higher it flies, so a pass reads in depth.

moments.about: Choreography of the scene's moments and cues. Timeline values are seconds after the moment arrives; -1 means the step does not happen for that kind. Every client plays the same schedule: whistle, the scoring section surging (crowd), the light-bank strobe (lighting), particles off the rim, the banner (broadcast), the PA chime, settle. Crowd: a cue's `crowd` is stand, clap, final (winners' sections stand to the end, losers' sit for `seconds`) or none; a timeline's standSeconds/groanSeconds say how long the side that scored or took the ball stands and the side that lost it groans (-1: not at all).

banner.about: Contract for Broadcast/Experience, which draw the banner: how big and how long, so the TOUCHDOWN reads as the moment and not as a chip. Angular sizes are at the wearer's eye. dwellSeconds is how long it stays up when nothing interrupts it; the next snap takes it down early, but never before minSeconds, so a quick snap shortens it rather than flashing it.

audio.about: Every sound is synthesised by tools/audio/build.py and normalised per class (loudness); the mix is gains (dB). assets name the .caf the headset plays; the .ogg twin beside it is for the web and Android. Ids ending Bed loop.

shaderGraph.about: Shader Graph materials authored as text in tools/shadergraph and compiled into assets by tools/shadergraph/build.py (docs/SHADERGRAPH.md). Each entry names the compiled file and prim, the parameters a renderer sets from these values, and a fallback: what a client without Shader Graph (web, Android, a failed load) draws instead.
